correctness.rationale: The invertible cumulative path map L sends K_{d+1}=conv(e_i-e_j) in the root hyperplane to P_a, with L^-1 x=(-x1/a1, x1/a1-x2/a2, ..., xd/ad). Supporting facets of K_n are exactly nonempty proper subset cuts sum_{i in S}z_i<=1; each equality face spans dimension d-1 because all bipartite crossing roots lie there. Mapping chosen complement pairs by indicator flips yields |u_T.x|<=1 with each nonzero T irredundant and ||u_T||^2=sum_{i in T}a_i^-2. The unique full-flip normal gives minimal facet distance and two centered contacts; ball feasibility for every T gives the entire center polytope, with codimension one from tight opposite full-flip pair and strict slack on other faces. Root vertices are interval vectors; the longest weighted interval gives exactly two farthest antipodes. Coordinate-permutation symmetry of K_n forces unique optimal John/Loewner ellipsoids to be root-space spheres; subset-normal length squared k(n-k)/n gives their constants n/F and 2. Symmetrizing an arbitrary ellipsoid B with operator convex matrix inversion proves optimal affine containment ratio sqrt(2F/n); Cauchy-Schwarz proves R/r>=d. Independent rational d=2..5 checks directly confirmed 56 facets and norms. All d>=2/a_i>0 follow analytically.

value.rationale: The weighted staircase simplex is canonical in triangulation geometry; its symmetric difference body is a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary slice. The exact facet-distance multiset and entire (d-1)-dimensional incenter locus despite just two tangent facets yield an unusual structural metric classification, and all weights exhibit a fixed optimal affine shape but arbitrarily bad Euclidean radius ratio. That contrast goes beyond a textbook facet count or weight substitution.

final_claim: For d>=2, positive weights a_i, difference body P_a=conv{v_i-v_j} of weighted orthoscheme simplex has precisely 2(2^d-1) facet halfspaces |u_T.x|<=1 indexed by nonempty flip subsets, distances (sum_{i in T} a_i^-2)^-1/2, unique circumcenter 0 with R=sqrt(sum a_i^2), inradius r=(sum a_i^-2)^-1/2 and an explicit (d-1)-dimensional full center polytope; John/Loewner ellipsoids and affine BM factor sqrt(2 floor((d+1)^2/4)/(d+1)) explicit.
limitations: d>=2, strictly positive a_i; Euclidean metric fixed in weighted x coordinates; John and Loewner ellipsoids depend on affine transform, but Euclidean radii do not; no zero-weight or arbitrary pair of staircase simplices.
